findings.title: packages/db/tests/pack-shaped-knowledge-read-census.test.mjs's executors() re-implements f-a2-grants.test.mjs's executors()
findings.evidence: pack-shaped-knowledge-read-census.test.mjs:63-72 defines `async function executors(query, signature) { const r = await query(\`select r.rolname from pg_roles r where r.rolname like 'clara%' and has_function_privilege(r.rolname, $1::regprocedure, 'EXECUTE') order by r.rolname\`, [signature]); return r.rows.map((x) => x.rolname); }`. packages/db/tests/f-a2-grants.test.mjs:42-49 already defines the identical query, hardcoded to rootQuery instead of taking a query parameter: `async function executors(signature) { const r = await rootQuery(...same SQL...); return r.rows.map((x) => x.rolname); }`. The new file's own header (lines 26-28) explicitly names f-a2-grants.test.mjs's executors() as 'the same instrument', showing the duplication was noticed, not missed.
findings.required_fix: Fowler 'Duplicated Code' -> extract the shared shape. The only real difference is that pack-shaped-knowledge-read-census.test.mjs needs a caller-supplied query (rootQuery by default, or a transaction-scoped client for the pkc.3 CONTROL cell) so an uncommitted GRANT is visible to the same probe. A single shared helper in rig-fixtures.mjs or rig-helpers.mjs taking `(signature, query = rootQuery)` would serve both files and remove the second copy. This is a judgement call, not a hard violation -- the two files import from different fixture modules (rig-helpers.mjs vs rig-fixtures.mjs) and the duplication is small (10 lines) and already justified in the file's own comments.

notes.note: 0243's implementation stamps clara.audit_log.actor_role from a new BEFORE INSERT trigger on the table (clara._tf_audit_actor_role) rather than from clara._audit itself, which is what the owner ruling's literal 'Key interfaces' text names ('clara._audit ... gains the actor's rank'). This is NOT a standards violation: it is compelled by a documented, machine-enforced repo law that outranks the ruling's wording -- clara._audit is ordinal 10 of the frozen metric_input_snapshot v1 producer closure (clara.metric_input_producer_version_members / clara.verify_metric_input_producer_freeze()), and scripts/migrate.mjs's FREEZE_GUARDS refuse any migration that recuts a member. The migration's own header (0243:25-43) states this was measured, not assumed: 'an earlier draft of this file DID recut _audit and the runner rolled the whole migration back'. Re-verified live in this review: clara._audit's prosrc sha256 (000c730cd2...) is byte-identical to the pin in both 0243's prestate and tail, and clara.verify_metric_input_producer_freeze() raises no exception on the lane database. The trigger approach is also strictly WIDER than the literal recut would have been (it reaches the table's whole write path, not one function), and 0243's own tail proves the acceptance criteria the ruling actually asked for (one writer; 304 callers unchanged; a door from an untouched lane, clara.create_client, inherits the column with no per-door edit) -- all reconfirmed live in this review. This is exactly the code-review skill's own rule that 'a documented repo standard overrides' a baseline expectation; it is flagged here only as a note for the Spec-axis reviewer, since the deviation is against the ruling's literal interface wording rather than against any documented coding standard.

All four migrations were read in full against the house migration law (header, prestate with measured prosrc/shape pins, idempotent-under-#957-redo statements, tail assertions re-measuring row counts/CHECKs/grants/RLS/trigger posture, preintegration-gate module, rig-meta cohort, gate-chain entry) and every specific numeric or hash claim in 0243 (the ticket the task flagged for extra scrutiny) was independently re-measured live on the lane database and matched exactly: the actor_role column, the 66,898 untouched NULL rows, the single clara._audit writer, the 304 unchanged callers, the byte-identical frozen clara._audit body, and a passing clara.verify_metric_input_producer_freeze(). TDD process was checked commit-by-commit: no horizontal slicing (a battery of red tests landing before implementation) was found anywhere in the range: every test-only commit extends a battery whose subject already exists from an earlier commit in the same ticket, and every test reads through a public interface (a governed SQL door or the table's own committed write, which this repo's documented rig idiom treats as the seam for a DB migration's own effect) with expected values coming from independently-minted fixtures or measured pins, never from re-deriving what the code computes. Shared files (CONTEXT.md, en.json, package.json, rig-meta.mjs, x42-s5-helpers.mjs, manifest.txt) were all touched minimally and at a sensible position. No PRD/ARCHITECTURE edit, no edit to an already-applied migration, and lint is clean on every touched file. One minor, judgement-call smell (Duplicated Code) is reported. Verdict: accept.
